raw_case_text: A 14-year-old male child presented with fever associated with chills of 3 days duration. He also had dull aching continuous holocranial headache associated with 3-4 episodes of vomiting. On the 3rd day of fever, he noticed giddiness associated with difficulty in sitting and standing; needing support of family members; and swaying while walking. There was blurring of vision but no dysphagia, dysarthria, weakness or incoordination of limbs, sensory symptoms, or myoclonic jerks. On examination, his vitals were stable. He was conscious and oriented. The speech was normal. Pupils were equal and reactive. Oculomotor abnormality in the form of sudden conjugate horizontal saccadic oscillations without intersaccadic interval (ocular flutter) occurring spontaneously, with eyes open and closed, during pursuit and saccades, and mainly in horizontal than vertical direction of gaze was seen [Video 1]. Other cranial nerves were normal. Motor examination showed normal tone and muscle power with sluggish deep tendon reflexes. Sensory examination was normal. He had titubation with truncal, stance, and gait ataxia. Plantar response was mute. Other system examination showed mild hepatosplenomegaly. Complete hemogram showed low platelet count (0.76 lakh). Liver function test showed transaminitis (aspartate aminotransferase: 110 IU/L; alanine aminotransferase: 156 IU/L). Serum dengue nonstructural 1 antigen and immunoglobulin M antibodies were positive. Magnetic resonance imaging brain plain was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis was normal. He was treated with antipyretics and intravenous fluids. His fever subsided, but ocular flutter and ataxia persisted. He was given 5 days course of intravenous methylprednisolone after fever subsided. The patient had symptomatic improvement in the form that his ataxia improved and ocular flutter decreased [Video 2]. He was able to walk without support and was discharged with tapering dose of oral steroids.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 14-year-old boy presented with a 3-day history of fever with chills, holocranial headache, and vomiting, complicated on day 3 by giddiness, blurred vision, involuntary eye oscillations, and severe truncal and gait ataxia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed fever with chills, continuous dull holocranial headache, and 3-4 episodes of vomiting over 3 days. On day 3 of fever, he acutely developed dizziness, blurred vision, inability to sit or stand without support, and swaying while walking.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, holocranial headache, vomiting, giddiness, blurred vision, and gait/postural instability. Negative for dysphagia, dysarthria, limb weakness or incoordination, sensory symptoms, or myoclonic jerks.

objective.physical_examination: Stable vital signs, conscious, oriented, normal speech, equal reactive pupils, and mild hepatosplenomegaly. Neurological exam revealed spontaneous conjugate horizontal saccadic oscillations without an intersaccadic interval (ocular flutter) present with eyes open and closed and during pursuit/saccades, accompanied by titubation and truncal, stance, and gait ataxia; other cranial nerves, motor tone/power, and sensation were normal, with sluggish deep tendon reflexes and mute plantar responses.
objective.routine_investigations: Thrombocytopenia (platelet count 0.76 lakh/mm3) and hepatic transaminitis (AST 110 IU/L, ALT 156 IU/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Plain brain MRI and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis were both normal.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Dengue-associated para-infectious ocular flutter and truncal/gait ataxia, confirmed by positive serum dengue NS1 antigen and dengue IgM antibodies with normal brain MRI and CSF. Initial fever resolved with antipyretics and IV fluids, and persistent ocular flutter and ataxia responded rapidly to a 5-day course of IV methylprednisolone, allowing independent ambulation and discharge on a tapering oral steroid regimen.
